text:
🗞 BEAT THE STREET BULLETIN 🗞
Date: 29 SEPTEMBER 2026
Telegram: [https://t.me/BeatTheStreetnews]

📍 ORDER WIN

KPI GREEN ENERGY LIMITED: Wins ₹2,025 Cr turnkey EPC order for a 500 MW/550 MWp solar PV project in Rajasthan.

STL NETWORKS LIMITED: Emerges as L1 bidder for a ₹249.8 Cr RailTel order for cloud infrastructure design, supply, installation, integration and deployment.

ARISINFRA SOLUTIONS LIMITED: Secures ₹400 Cr DaaS mandate for Transcon UNO commercial redevelopment project at Kalina, Mumbai.

JNK INDIA: Wins two significant orders from an Indian customer for supply and installation, commissioning and testing of a Flare Package, classified as a ₹0–100 Cr project.

ACCORD TRANSFORMER & SWITCHGEAR: Wins orders worth ₹8.64 Cr, including ₹8.39 Cr for electrical transformers and ₹24.50 Lakh for an inverter duty transformer.

SUGS LLOYD: Wins ₹8.90 Cr solar power project order from Sachkhand Sri Harmander Sahib for a 2 MW ground-mounted solar project.

KRYSTAL INTEGRATED SERVICES LIMITED: Wins ₹8.75 Cr manpower services contract from Kosol Energie for its Gujarat factory for one year.

ITCONS E-SOLUTIONS: Wins ~₹6.94 Cr contract from UP Power Transmission Corporation for deployment of 114 resources over two years.

PANACHE DIGILIFE LIMITED: Subsidiary Panache Newage Technology receives a telecom work order for installation, configuration, technical services, equipment and real-time monitoring for approximately 36 months.

DHRUV CONSULTANCY SERVICES LIMITED: Receives ₹3.79 Cr LOA from Maharashtra PWD for consultancy services on an ADB-funded road development project.

SHAYONA ENGINEERING LIMITED: Receives ₹19.76 Lakh purchase order for industrial piping solutions from a domestic customer.

📍 ACQUISITION

ENDURANCE TECHNOLOGIES LIMITED: Wholly owned subsidiary Endurance Overseas SpA to acquire the remaining 32% stake in Stöferle Automotive GmbH and Stöferle GmbH, Germany, for €18 Mn.

KRONOX LAB SCIENCES LIMITED: Indo Borax & Chemicals acquires 2.3844 Cr shares, representing a 64.26% stake, through block deals at ₹103.22 per share.

COSMO FIRST: Zigly Pet Care acquires Prolife Specialty Vet Clinic in Mumbai, marking its third strategic veterinary clinic acquisition.

SAR TELEVENTURE LIMITED: Acquires 1.708 Cr shares of Tikona Communication, taking its stake to 70.17%.

GEMENVIRO: Step-down subsidiary proposes to acquire Solluz Energy Private Limited, with completion expected by March 31, 2027.

INDO BORAX & CHEMICALS LIMITED: Step-down subsidiary completes acquisition of a 64.26% stake in Kronox Lab Sciences Limited.

UMIYA HOLDING PRIVATE LIMITED: Acquires 500 shares of Umiya Buildcon Limited through the open market, with holding remaining at 38.84%.

📍 COLLABORATION

EP BIOCOMPOSITES: Signs strategic collaboration with Malligavad Foundation for lake, creek, wetland restoration, water conservation, effluent treatment and eco-restoration projects across multiple regions.

QUEST LABORATORIES: Enters strategic collaboration with Niraga Capitals for international expansion, strategic partnerships, business development, M&A and capital-raising initiatives.

PINE LABS: Extends its five-year technology partnership with Woolworths Group to strengthen digital gift-card infrastructure and platform integration.

NLC INDIA LIMITED: Board approves 50:50 JV with NALCO for development of a 1,080 MW Thermal Captive Power Plant.

📍 LEADERSHIP CHANGES

VIKRAM SOLAR LIMITED: Rony Banerjee resigns as Executive Vice President–Sales & BD, while Nimish Jain is appointed Chief Business Officer, effective September 28, 2026.

DIXON TECHNOLOGIES: Board approves re-appointment of Sunil Vachani as Whole Time Director and Atul B. Lall as Managing Director for five years from May 5, 2027.

KRONOX LAB SCIENCES: Board reconstitutes key committees, appointing Dhananjay Tapasvi, Anuradha Suneet Maheshwari and Suresh Kalra as respective committee chairpersons.

FOURTH GENERATION INFORMATION SYSTEMS LIMITED: Re-appoints Srivenkata Ramana Tammisetti as Director and regularizes Padmini Biradar as Independent Non-Executive Director for a five-year term.

PANYAM CEMENTS: Appoints Sunki Reddy Pitchi Reddy as Chief Financial Officer effective September 29, 2026.

STANDARD CAPITAL MARKETS: Ram Gopal Jindal resigns as Managing Director but continues as Executive Director and remains on the Board.

COAL INDIA LIMITED: Dr. Anjani Kumar relinquishes charge as Executive Director–Contracts following his appointment as Director (Tech.) at Western Coalfields.

TECHNOCRAFT INDUSTRIES: Announces internal role and designation changes for nine Senior Management Personnel effective October 1, 2026.

UNITED SPIRITS LIMITED: Executive Vice President and Financial Controller Nimish Shah resigns effective October 12, 2026 to pursue an opportunity outside the company.

SAI SILKS (KALAMANDIR) LIMITED: Appoints Shilpa Kotagiri as Company Secretary and Compliance Officer effective October 1, 2026.

CG-VAK SOFTWARE AND EXPORTS LIMITED: Three Independent Directors cease office on completion of their prescribed tenure on September 28, 2026.

📍 NEW PROJECTS

EXIDE INDUSTRIES: Invests ₹99.99 Cr in subsidiary Exide Energy Solutions to fund a greenfield Bengaluru plant for lithium-ion battery cells, modules and packs.

GODAWARI POWER & ISPAT: Approves ₹50 Cr investment in Godawari New Energy for capex and working capital requirements of its Battery Energy Storage System plant.

NAVIN FLUORINE: Successfully commissions debottlenecking capacity at its Multi Purpose Plant at Dahej, with commercial production and dispatch commencing.

HGINFRA: Receives financial closure for its ₹1,582.11 Cr Gobindpur–Tangi six-lane highway project from NHAI.

📍 FUNDRAISING

IRB INVIT FUND: Completes ₹2,351 Cr fund raise through ₹2,000 Cr QIP and ₹351 Cr preferential allotment to support acquisition of two highway assets.

INTERISE TRUST: Approves allotment of Series I, II and III debentures aggregating ₹1,737 Cr, to be listed on BSE.

BHARAT PARENTERALS: Board approves issuance of up to 9,12,759 equity shares to 15 non-promoter investors to raise ₹138.99 Cr.

CAPITAL INDIA FINANCE LIMITED: Raises ₹100 Cr through secured NCDs carrying a fixed 10% annual coupon and maturing on December 29, 2028.

TUBE INVESTMENTS OF INDIA: Subscribes ₹250 Cr to CCPS of subsidiary TI Clean Mobility to support expansion of its electric mobility operations.

PRAXIS HOME RETAIL LIMITED: Enters agreement for an unsecured inter-corporate loan of up to ₹2.50 Cr from Matrix Park for working capital and general corporate purposes.

📍 CREDIT RATINGS

ADITYA BIRLA CAPITAL: India Ratings affirms Long-Term Issuer Rating at IND AAA/Stable and Commercial Paper rating at IND A1+.

SIS LIMITED: CRISIL reaffirms AA- rating and revises the outlook on ₹250 Cr NCDs from Stable to Positive; short-term rating remains A1+.

SAURASHTRA CEMENT LIMITED: ICRA reaffirms BBB-/Stable rating on instruments aggregating ₹404 Cr.

KALYANI STEELS LIMITED: ICRA reaffirms A1+ rating on ₹75 Cr Commercial Paper.

📍 FII STAKE CHANGES / BOUGHT-SOLD

BLUESTONE JEWELLERY AND LIFESTYLE LIMITED: 360 One Alternates Asset Management sells 35,13,672 equity shares through the open market on September 24, 2026.

ALEMBIC PHARMA: DSP group entities report a 0.07 percentage-point reduction in holding to 2.97% following open-market transactions.

FAMILY CARE HOSPITALS LIMITED: Dr. Sowmya Deshpande sells 5,49,989 shares worth ₹54.01 Cr through the open market between August 15 and September 28, 2026.

KAPSTON SERVICES: Kalyan Ram Nandamuri, family members and associates acquire 15 lakh promoter-held shares through bulk deals.

📍 IPO

No new IPO-specific update reported.

📍 Q2 / BUSINESS UPDATE

DR REDDYS LABORATORIES: Says Brazil is emerging as a larger market, plans 20–25 US launches in FY27 and expects FDA approval for Abatacept after December.

VINATI ORGANICS: Says rupee depreciation is aiding realisations, expects ATBS demand to pick up in December and sees ₹500–550 Cr maximum revenue potential from Veeral Organics.

CLSA ON INDIAN AUTOS: Says auto demand remains resilient, with festive-season growth expected at mid-to-high single digits despite a high base.

CLSA ON INDIAN AUTOS: Says electrification outlook is improving across two-wheelers and passenger vehicles, while cost inflation continues to pressure entry-level vehicle margins.

NOMURA: Says most raw-material prices softened or remained range-bound in September, though several input costs remain elevated YoY/QoQ.

EQUITAS SFB: Estimates a potential ₹25–30 Cr revenue impact from the IRDAI proposal.

📍 USFDA / REGULATORY

SYMBIOTEC: Receives Establishment Inspection Report from US FDA for its Pithampur facility with Voluntary Action Indicated status following the August inspection.

SUN PHARMA, CIPLA, BIOCON, ZYDUS LIFE, HESTER BIO AND SHILPA: Certain speciality drugs and associated ingredients imported from India and 19 other countries will not face US ad valorem tariffs for rare-disease treatments.

📍 CLARIFICATION

FORTIS HEALTHCARE: IHH says it will cooperate with the forensic audit proceedings and reiterates its 2018 acquisition of Fortis followed a competitive bidding process and required approvals.

KALPATARU PROJECTS INTERNATIONAL LIMITED: Delhi High Court upholds an earlier order involving an arbitral award concerning JV Kurukshetra Expressway, with the company considering further legal steps.

📍 LAUNCHES

HEXAGON NUTRITION: Completes commercial-scale process validation of PFH-VAP, a stable Vitamin A Palmitate formulation proposed to be marketed internationally as VIT A+.

📍 INCORPORATE / CORPORATE STRUCTURE

SOLAR INDUSTRIES: Wholly owned subsidiary Solar Overseas Mauritius incorporates Solar Explochem Proprietary Limited in Botswana with USD 325,000 initial capital for a 65% shareholding.

BLUESPRING ENTERPRISES LIMITED: Wholly owned subsidiary Bluspring New Horizon Two to amalgamate with LSG Sky Chefs India under Section 233 of the Companies Act, streamlining the group structure.

📍 IT NEWS

PINE LABS: Extends technology partnership with Woolworths Group to enhance API-led gift-card infrastructure and integration with wider commerce ecosystems.

📍 TAX ORDER

TATASTEEL: Favourable ITAT orders for FY2008 and FY2009 reduce tax exposure by ₹642 Cr, from approximately ₹1,901 Cr to ₹1,259 Cr.

PANACEA BIOTEC LIMITED: Income Tax Department imposes penalties of approximately ₹4.32 Cr for AY2022-23 and AY2023-24; company plans to appeal.

HP COTTON TEXTILE MILLS: Pays ₹7.29 Lakh under Haryana's One Time Settlement Scheme against original tax demand of ₹21.20 Lakh for FY2015-16 to FY2017-18.

📍 OTHERS

ARTEMIS HOSPITALS: Receives CGST Gurugram show cause notice alleging GST non-remittance on medicines, consumables and implants, with potential implications of ₹11.11 Cr plus interest and penalty.

MCLEOD RUSSEL INDIA LIMITED: Signs Master Restructuring Agreement with NARCL and Aditya Khaitan to restructure outstanding debt of ₹2,483.31 Cr.

ADVIT JEWELS LIMITED: Signs nine-year lease for approximately 2,200 sq ft commercial premises in Defence Colony, New Delhi, with rent starting at ₹8.50 Lakh per month.

BGR ENERGY: NCLAT adjourns insolvency appeal to November 16 while noting a settlement proposal with NARCL and extends the suspension order.

ZENLABS ETHICA LIMITED: Members re-appoint N. Kumar Chabbra & Co. as Statutory Auditors for five years at the 33rd AGM.

THE GREAT EASTERN SHIPPING COMPANY: Buys back 1,797 equity shares at an average price of ₹1,530 per share.

ADVANCED ENZYME TECHNOLOGIES: Buys back 25,000 equity shares at an average price of ₹283.6025 per share.

MINDA CORPORATION: Issues ₹100 Cr Commercial Paper listed on NSE, with redemption scheduled for December 28, 2026.

JYOTHY LABS: Receives ₹6.63 Cr insurance claim against a ₹7.33 Cr settled claim related to a fire at its Patiala warehouse.

VARDHMAN POLYTEX: Repays ₹1.50 Cr towards secured OCDs, reducing aggregate principal outstanding to ₹10.98 Cr.

EMBASSY REIT: Trading window closes from September 30, 2026 until 48 hours after declaration of September-quarter and half-year results.

CHATHA FOODS: Receives BSE listing approval for 16,000 equity shares allotted to promoters pursuant to warrant conversion.

PVR INOX: Accepts 95,907 equity shares in its buyback offer, with promoter/PAC holding rising from 27.53% to 27.60% post-buyback.

SANOFI: Receives ₹16.40 Cr GST show cause notice from Gujarat State Tax Officer concerning FY2022-23; company is preparing its response.

PIRAMAL PHARMA: Receives ₹4.06 Cr GST demand plus equivalent penalty related to input tax credit matters and plans to appeal.

TVS SRICHAKRA: Receives state tax show cause notice proposing ₹17.53 Cr demand including tax, interest and penalty over alleged excess ITC availment.

HI-PRINT ELECTROMACK: Files SEBI SAST disclosure regarding inter-se transfer of shares among promoters.

SIYARAM RECYCLING INDUSTRIES: Receives “Excellence in Brass Recycling” award at the International Dazzling Awards.

IRB INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPERS: Executes project implementation agreements with IRB InvIT Fund covering two tollway SPVs with aggregate balance concession value of approximately ₹2,663 Cr.

HERMES LIMITED: Reports preferential allotment of 14.025 Cr warrants to Hermes and 22.525 Cr warrants to PACs, convertible into equity shares.

SAI SILKS (KALAMANDIR) LIMITED: Revises use of ₹20.27 Cr of IPO proceeds from warehouses to new stores by March 31, 2027.

ASUTOSH ENTERPRISES LIMITED: Appoints Rinku Gupta & Associates as Secretarial Auditor for five years from FY2026-27 to FY2030-31.

MYSORE PAPER MILLS: Board approves unaudited financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026.

GODAWARI POWER & ISPAT: Approves ₹50 Cr investment in subsidiary Godawari New Energy for its Battery Energy Storage System plant.

INDIAN GOVERNMENT: Engages with China to explore Xinjiang airspace as an alternative route for Indian airlines amid continued Pakistan airspace restrictions.

IRAQ TRANSPORT MINISTRY: Says Iraqi Airways is preparing to resume flights to Iran in October after securing a special exemption.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA: Plans nationwide “Reform Express” campaign from October 2 to showcase announced reforms and reach targeted beneficiaries.

FED WATCH: Markets monitor Fed officials after the sharp rise in Treasury yields, while Deutsche Bank expects two additional 25-basis-point hikes in December and March.

AXIS CAPITAL ON EIH: Notes hotel pipeline revival and improving RevPAR outlook while maintaining its published BUY view and ₹385 target.

KOTAK ON OIL & GAS: Raises FY27E crude oil price assumption to US$90/bbl and maintains its published BUY view on ONGC with ₹355 fair value.

KOTAK ON ELECTRONIC MANUFACTURING SERVICES: Raises published fair values for Cyient DLM and Avalon Technologies while highlighting emerging semiconductor equipment opportunities.

AUGMONT ENTERPRISES: Says customers can sell, take delivery, pledge or obtain loans against gold held in vaults after conversion into EGRs.

DIXON TECHNOLOGIES : ROUTINE CORPORATE FILING REGARDING BOARD APPOINTMENTS

• Re-appointment of Mr. Sunil Vachani as Whole Time Director for 5 years from May 5, 2027.
• Re-appointment of Mr. Atul B. Lall as Managing Director for 5 years from May 5, 2027.
• Both directors are liable to retire by rotation.
• Full details enclosed as Annexure-A on website.
Impact: Neutral (Routine corporate filing regarding board appointments.)

JNK INDIA : WINS 2 ORDERS

• The company has received two significant orders from an Indian customer.
• Order 1 is for the supply of a Flare Package, including design, engineering, manufacture, procurement, and supply on a delivery-at-site basis in India.
• Order 2 is for services related to the flare package, encompassing installation, erection, pre-commissioning, commissioning, performance testing, and handover.
• Project classification is 'Significant' (₹0-100 Cr).
Impact: Positive (The company has secured new orders, indicating business growth and operational progress.)

VIKRAM SOLAR LIMITED : RESIGNATION OF SENIOR MANAGEMENT PERSONNEL (SMP)

• Rony Banerjee, Executive Vice President - Sales & BD, has resigned effective September 28, 2026.
• The company has accepted his resignation.
• Nimish Jain appointed as Chief Business Officer.
Impact: Neutral (Personnel change)

MCLEOD RUSSEL INDIA LIMITED : DEBT RESTRUCTURING AGREEMENT SIGNED

• McLeod Russel India Limited has entered into a Master Restructuring Agreement (MRA) with National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited (NARCL) and Mr. Aditya Khaitan.
• The agreement aims at restructuring the company's outstanding debt.
• Total outstanding debt is ₹2,483.31 Crore, comprising sustainable debt of ₹1,050 Crore and unsustainable debt of ₹1,433.31 Crore.
• Key terms include repayment of sustainable debt by FY2029, establishment of a monitoring committee, allotment of 10% equity shares with anti-dilution protection, pledge of promoter shareholding, and the right to appoint a Nominee Director.
• Mr. Aditya Khaitan is a promoter of the company and holds 17,272 equity shares.
Impact: Positive (Restructuring of debt to improve financial health)

ARTEMIS HOSPITALS RECEIVES SHOW CAUSE NOTICE FROM CGST GURUGRAM

• Company received a show cause notice dated September 28, 2026, from the Office of the Assistant Commissioner, CGST, Gurugram, concerning financial year 2022-23.
• The notice alleges that the company charged MRP on medicines, consumables, and implants while providing healthcare services, including GST, and did not remit it to the government.
• The period under review is from April 1, 2022, to March 31, 2023.
• Potential financial implications are estimated at ₹11.11 Crore plus interest and penalty.
• The company is filing a writ petition before the High Court of Punjab & Haryana, Chandigarh, to address this notice and link it with a previous writ where a stay has been granted.
• This follows a prior writ petition filed concerning a show cause notice for an earlier period on a similar matter.
Impact: Negative (Regulatory scrutiny over tax compliance and potential financial implications.)

POWER MECH PROJECTS: SECURES ₹549.37 CR O&M ORDER FROM ADANI GROUP COMPANY

• Company received order from Moxie Power Generation Limited, Adani Group.
• Order value: ₹549.37 crore, excluding GST.
• Scope includes complete Operations & Maintenance services for the 2×600 MW Moxie Power Generation Ltd Tuticorin Thermal Power Plant.
• Contract tenure: 60 months.
• Execution period: October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2031.
• Order is from a domestic entity and is not a related-party transaction.
Impact: Positive — sizeable 5-year O&M contract strengthens Power Mech’s recurring revenue visibility and thermal power services order book.

SOLAR INDUSTRIES: MAURITIUS SUBSIDIARY INCORPORATES BOTSWANA STEP-DOWN SUBSIDIARY

• Solar Overseas Mauritius Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, has incorporated Solar Explochem Proprietary Limited in Botswana.
• The incorporation took place on September 29, 2026.
• The new subsidiary is in the explosives industry.
• This move represents an expansion of business operations.
• Initial capital subscription was in cash, amounting to USD 325,000 for 65% shareholding.
Impact: Positive (Expansion of business operations into Botswana through a step-down subsidiary)

PANKAJ POLYMERS : STRENGTHENS DIGITAL COMMERCE ECOSYSTEM THROUGH PARTNERSHIPS

• Strategic partnerships to enable issuance, sale, and distribution of digital vouchers through its AI-enabled technology platform.
• Partnerships include companies like 99 Gifts, Hubble Money, Daalchini, Magicpin for B2C sales and Yoho, Blossom for D2C e-voucher issuance.
• The company aims to build a connected digital ecosystem for voucher issuance, distribution, and consumer engagement.
• This disclosure will be hosted on the company's website: https://www.rupiafin.com/investors/
Impact: Neutral (Routine disclosure of business partnerships)
Wells Fargo Investment Institute upgrades S&P 500 industrials sector to favorable from neutral.
Wells Fargo Investment Institute downgrades S&P 500 information technology sector to neutral from favorable.

HEXAGON NUTRITION : UNVEILS NEW STABLE VITAMIN A FORMULATION

• Company completes commercial-scale process validation of PFH-VAP, a stable formulation of Vitamin A Palmitate.
• Product proposed to be commercially marketed under the brand name “VIT A+” in international markets.
• Completion of process validation is a significant milestone for development and scale-up of PFH-VAP.
• Product intended for large-scale food fortification applications.
• Company will undertake necessary steps towards commercialisation of VIT A+.
Impact: Positive (Milestone achieved in product development for large-scale food fortification)
Wells Fargo Investment Institute forecasts US Fed policy rate at 4.75%-5.00% by 2027-end vs prior forecast of 4.00%-4.25%. 🔴🔴
Wells Fargo Investment Institute cuts gold's 2027 year-end target range to $5,200-$5,400 per ounce from prior forecast of $5,400-$5.600 per ounce.

KRONOX : BOARD RECONSTITUTES COMMITTEES

• Board reconstituted Audit Committee, Nomination & Remuneration Committee, Stakeholders Relationship Committee and Corporate Social Responsibility Committee.
• Mr. Dhananjay Tapasvi appointed Chairman of Audit Committee and Nomination and Remuneration Committee.
• Ms. Anuradha Suneet Maheshwari appointed Chairperson of Stakeholders Relationship Committee.
• Mr. Suresh Kalra appointed Chairperson of Corporate Social Responsibility Committee.
• Reconstitution effective September 29, 2026.
Impact: Neutral (Routine board committee restructuring following management changes.)
Wells Fargo Investment Institute forecasts 10-Year US Treasury yield at 5.25%-5.75% by 2027-end vs prior forecast of 4.50%-5.00%. 🔴🔴🔴🔴

ADVIT JEWELS LIMITED : LEASE DEED SIGNED FOR NEW DELHI PREMISES

• Company has entered into a lease deed with Mr. Charanjeet Singh for premises at D-32, Lala Lajpat Rai Marg, Defence Colony, New Delhi.
• The lease is for a period of nine years, commencing August 01, 2026 and ending on July 31, 2035.
• The premises, approximately 2,200 sq. ft. super built-up area, will be utilized for commercial business activities.
• The rent is ₹8,50,000 per month for the first three years, increasing to ₹9,77,500 for the next three, and ₹11,24,125 for the final three years.
• A refundable, interest-free security deposit of ₹25,50,000 has been paid.
• The lease deed was executed on September 28, 2026.
Impact: Positive (Lease facilitates company's business operations and expansion in New Delhi)

MACH TRAVEL SOLUTIONS LTD : RECOGNIZED AMONG LEADING SMES OF INDIA BY DUN & BRADSTREET

• Mach Travel Solutions Limited featured among 'Leading SMEs of India' in Dun & Bradstreet's Business Enterprises of Tomorrow 2026.
• The recognition was announced with the release of the report on September 29, 2026.
• Amit Bhatia, Chairman & Managing Director, stated, “We are pleased to be featured among the ‘Leading SMEs of India' in Dun & Bradstreet's Business Enterprises of Tomorrow 2026. This recognition is encouraging for us as we continue to build and strengthen the organisation for its next phase of growth.”
• The company provides technology-enabled end-to-end travel solutions across Corporate Travel, MICE, B2B, Leisure and Government & Institutional Projects.
• Mach Travel Solutions is also developing its B2C Online Travel Agency platform, Machtravel.com.
Impact: Positive (Industry recognition for leadership among SMEs)
SILGO RETAIL LIMITED : PROMOTER INTER-SE TRANSFER OF 93,750 SHARES AT ₹69.25

SAURASHTRA CEMENT LTD : CREDIT RATING RE-AFFIRMED

• ICRA Limited has re-affirmed the long-term credit rating of BBB- (Stable) for Saurashtra Cement Limited's instruments.
• The total rated amount aggregates to ₹404.00 crore.
• Instruments include long-term fund-based term loans (₹31.95 crore), non-fund-based facilities (₹340.00 crore), cash credit (₹20.00 crore), and unallocated limits (₹12.05 crore).
Impact: Neutral

PRAXIS HOME RETAIL LTD : ENTERS UNSECURED LOAN AGREEMENT WORTH RS 2.50 CR

• Loan agreement executed on September 29, 2026, with Matrix Park Private Limited.
• Unsecured inter-corporate loan of up to ₹2.50 Crore to be availed on or before March 31, 2027.
• Loan is for working capital requirement and general corporate purpose.
• Interest rate at 13% per annum for a tenure of 6 months, subject to mutual written agreement for extension.
• Company had previously availed an unsecured inter-corporate loan of ₹3.50 Crore from Matrix Park Private Limited on September 25, 2026.
• Aggregate amount of loans availed from and outstanding to Matrix Park Private Limited will be ₹6.00 Crore.
Impact: Positive (Secures working capital and general corporate funding)

ZENLABS ETHICA LTD. : RE-APPOINTS STATUTORY AUDITORS

• Members of the company re-appointed M/s. N. Kumar Chabbra & Co., Chartered Accountants as Statutory Auditors for a term of five years at the 33rd AGM held on September 29, 2026.
• M/s. N. Kumar Chabbra & Co. (Firm Registration No. 000873N) are professional Chartered Accountants with experience in audit and assurance, taxation, and advisory services.
• The firm holds a valid Peer Review Certificate and has confirmed its eligibility for re-appointment.
Impact: Positive (Continuation of existing auditors provides stability and continuity in financial reporting.)

GEMENVIRO: GEMENVIRO'S STEP-DOWN SUBSIDIARY TO ACQUIRE SOLLUZ ENERGY PRIVATE LIMITED

• Proposed investment in Solluz Energy Private Limited is expected to be completed on or before March 31, 2027.
• The timeline considers ongoing procedural formalities.
Impact: Positive (Furtherance of corporate strategy regarding investment in Solluz Energy Private Limited.)

BGR ENERGY : INSOLVENCY PROCEEDINGS ADJOURNED TO NOV 16

• The appeal filed before the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) came up for hearing on 28th September 2026.
• The Tribunal adjourned the matter to 16th November 2026, taking note of a settlement proposal with NARCL.
• The suspension order granted by NCLAT has been extended until the next hearing.
• The company is awaiting the official order copy and will inform the stock exchanges upon receipt.

Impact: Neutral (Procedural update on insolvency proceedings; matter adjourned pending settlement proposal.)

JYOTHY LABS : FIRE INCIDENT - INSURANCE CLAIM SETTLED

• Insurance claim of ₹7.33 crore from the fire incident at the C&FA operated warehouse at Patiala, Punjab has been settled by ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Limited.
• The company has received the insurance claim amount of ₹6.63 crores today.
• Alternate warehousing facilities were arranged to ensure continuity of business operations without material disruption.
• No other material financial impact on the company other than the claim amount.
Impact: Neutral (Insurance claim settled, no material financial impact beyond the claim amount.)

MINDA CORPORATION LIMITED ISSUED RS 100 CR COMMERCIAL PAPER

• Commercial Paper listed on NSE on Sep 29, 2026.
• Size of issue: INR 100 crores. Redemption date: Dec 28, 2026.
Impact: Neutral (Routine corporate debt issuance)

THE GREAT EASTERN SHIPPING COMPANY LIMITED: ROUTINE BUYBACK OF EQUITY SHARES

• The company bought back 1,797 equity shares at an average price of ₹1530.00 per share.
• Cumulative shares bought back as of September 29, 2026, are 18,58,941.
Impact: Neutral (Routine buyback disclosure)

MUTHOOT CAPITAL SERVICES : PRIOR INTIMATION OF BOARD MEETING

• Meeting of the Debenture Issue and Allotment Committee of the Board of Directors to be held on Saturday, October 03, 2026.
• Committee will consider and approve the proposed issuance of Non-Convertible Debentures ("NCDs") on a private placement basis, within the overall limits approved by the Board of Directors and shareholders.
• Filing for BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited.

EMBASSY REIT : TRADING WINDOW CLOSURE FOR SEPT 30, 2026 QUARTER

• Trading window for designated persons and their immediate relatives to close from September 30, 2026.
• Window to remain closed until 48 hours after the declaration of financial results for the quarter and half-year ended September 30, 2026.
• Pursuant to SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 and the code on unpublished price sensitive information.

BLUESTONE JEWELLERY AND LIFESTYLE LIMITED : DISCLOSURE RECEIVED UNDER REGULATION 29(2) OF SEBI

• The company received a disclosure dated September 28, 2026, from 360 One Alternates Asset Management Limited.
• The disclosure pertains to the sale of 35,13,672 equity shares of the company.
• The sale occurred through the open market on September 24, 2026.
• The disclosure was made pursuant to Regulation 29(2) of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011.
Impact: Neutral (Disclosure of shareholding change as per regulatory requirements)

VARDHMAN POLYTEX LTD : PART REPAYMENT TOWARDS OCDS

• Company made a payment of Rs.1,50,00,000/- towards part repayment of secured, unlisted, redeemable and optionally convertible debentures (“OCDs”)
• Payment was effected by way of pro-rata reduction in the face value/principal amount of each of the 1,500 outstanding OCDs
• Face value/principal per OCD reduced from Rs.83,225.39 to Rs.73,225.39

INDIA BATTERY STORAGE | DEMAND SURGES, IMPORT DEPENDENCE REMAINS

Storage Demand
- H1 2025 installations: ~98 MWh.
- H1 2026 installations: 8.2 GWh.
- Storage installations increased ~84x YoY.
- FY27–FY28 additions estimated at 45–50 GWh.
- Wood Mackenzie estimates 260 GWh tender pipeline.

Domestic Cell Capacity
- India had ~2 GWh operational cell capacity in August.
- Capacity covers less than 1% of pipeline.
- Exide's 6 GWh line is not yet commercial.
- Domestic supply remains far below expected demand.
- Imports therefore fill the supply gap.

Import Dependence
- FY26 Li-ion battery imports: ~$4.7 Bn.
- Imports increased 57% YoY.
- China accounted for ~83.6% of imports.
- Heavy dependence exposes developers to external pricing.

Battery Cost Pressure
- Chinese storage cell prices rose 22% in six months.
- Battery costs reached ~$70–75/kWh in 2026.
- 2025 costs were ~$50–55/kWh.
- Developers typically buy batteries ~1 year after bids.
- Older tariffs can therefore face higher input costs.
- Crisil flags ~12 GWh with weak returns.

Technology Access Challenge
- China restricted LFP cathode technology exports.
- Exporting the technology now requires a licence.
- Licensing access is becoming more difficult.
- Amara Raja shifted toward developing its own technology.
- Management cited limited Chinese technology sharing.

India's Cell Manufacturing Push
- India has announced 226 GWh capacity through 2035.
- PLI ACC scheme awarded 40 GWh.
- Only ~1.4 GWh was operational by February 2026.
- No PLI incentives had been paid by then.
- Ola Electric has 2.5 GWh operational capacity.
- Amara Raja targets its first 2 GWh line in 2027.
- Agratas targets 20 GWh at Sanand.
- Agratas expects output to begin in 2027.

JSW Technology Development
- JSW is pursuing in-house cell technology.
- Management estimates development could take 1–2 years.
- JSW Projects partnered with COEP Tech.
- Battery R&D centre planned in Pune.
- Over ₹800 Cr committed across two phases.
- Phase 1 focuses on cell design and prototypes.
- Phase 2 targets 100–600 Ah cell validation.

Exide Technology
- Exide commissioned a 6 GWh plant.
- Plant uses SVOLT technology.
- Technology agreement was signed in March 2022.
- Agreement predates recent export restrictions.

Battery Materials Opportunity
- Gujarat Fluorochemicals supplies LiPF6 commercially.
- LFP cathode qualification expected by Q3 FY27.
- Himadri plans 40,000 TPA LFP capacity.
- Initial 2,000 TPA targeted by Q3 FY27.
- Neogen committed ₹1,795 Cr to battery chemicals.
- Electrolyte production targeted for H1 FY27.

Key Constraints
- Restricted technology does not mean completely banned.
- Export licences can still be granted.
- Domestic cells cost 25–40% more currently.
- China's broader equipment controls remain suspended.
- Current suspension runs until November 10, 2026.

KEY TAKEAWAY
India's battery-storage demand is expanding rapidly, but domestic cell manufacturing remains far behind the emerging requirement. The key opportunity is shifting from simply importing cells toward developing domestic technology, cell manufacturing and the wider battery-materials ecosystem.

SPACEX STARSHIP | FIRST ORBITAL FLIGHT + STARLINK DEPLOYMENT

Historic Milestone
- Starship reached orbit for the first time.
- Mission launched from SpaceX Starbase.
- Vehicle stands nearly 40 storeys tall.
- Super Heavy booster powered the ascent.
- Booster later splashed down in the Gulf.
- Starship became the primary orbital vehicle.

Engine Setback
- One main engine shut down early.
- Initial assessment suggested orbit might be impossible.
- Engineers later confirmed an orbital attempt remained possible.
- Starship successfully performed the required engine firing.
- Vehicle subsequently reached orbit.

Starlink Satellite Deployment
- Starship deployed 26 next-generation Starlink satellites.
- Satellites were deployed individually.
- Deployment occurred around 269 km altitude.
- This represents Starship's first orbital payload.
- V3 satellites reportedly offer much higher capacity.
- V3 can handle 10x more data than V2 mini.

Starship Development
- Starship is designed for full reusability.
- Previous 13 test flights remained suborbital.
- This mission represents the 14th test flight.
- Orbital capability is a major development milestone.
- Development has reportedly cost over $15 Bn.
- Routine Starship operations are targeted later this year.

Starlink Expansion
- Starship is designed to accelerate Starlink deployment.
- Current Falcon 9 launches smaller V2 mini batches.
- V3 satellites can carry significantly more data.
- Future Starship missions could launch 60 V3 satellites.
- Higher launch capacity can accelerate network expansion.
- Starlink remains central to Starship's commercial rationale.

Revenue Significance
- V3 deployment adds significant future network capacity.
- Analysts estimate substantial potential Starlink revenue impact.
- Higher satellite capacity supports additional customers.
- Starship could reduce launch costs over time.
- Frequent launches could improve Starlink expansion economics.

Reusability & Future Missions
- Latest mission includes a controlled return attempt.
- Re-entry requires a deorbit engine firing.
- Precise vehicle positioning is required.
- Final descent involves a controlled flip manoeuvre.
- Latest spacecraft recovery is not planned.
- Future missions aim for land recovery.

NASA Artemis
- Starship is central to NASA's Artemis plans.
- Artemis aims to return astronauts to the Moon.
- Long-term plans include sustained lunar presence.
- Lunar missions could support eventual Mars exploration.
- Starship is intended to support future lunar missions.

KEY TAKEAWAY
Starship's first orbital achievement and deployment of 26 V3 Starlink satellites mark a major step toward routine operations. The platform is intended to accelerate Starlink expansion, reduce launch costs through reusability and support future NASA Artemis missions.

The hidden chain, layer by layer
Where India stands across the actuator stack

HUMANOID ROBOTS | INDIA’S ACTUATOR SUPPLY-CHAIN OPPORTUNITY

Why Actuators Matter
- Humanoids can carry 40+ actuators.
- Actuators function like robotic muscles.
- Each joint needs controlled motion.
- Components combine motors, reducers and sensors.
- Precision requirements are extremely demanding.
- Actuators represent a major BOM opportunity.

Global Supply Chain
- Precision actuator supply remains concentrated globally.
- Japan dominates harmonic reducer technology.
- China has expanded commodity reducer capacity.
- Roller screws come from specialised global suppliers.
- Encoders remain concentrated among specialist manufacturers.
- Rare-earth magnets remain heavily China-dependent.
- Precision grinding equipment is also globally concentrated.

India’s Current Strengths
- India has strong precision machining capabilities.
- Automotive-scale gear manufacturing is established.
- Industrial bearing capabilities are well developed.
- Motor laminations and winding capabilities exist.
- Electronics assembly capabilities are available.
- These form the actuator’s manufacturing periphery.

Critical Gaps
- No disclosed Indian harmonic reducer manufacturer.
- No disclosed Indian encoder manufacturer.
- Robot-joint torque sensors remain absent.
- Cross-roller bearings remain a gap.
- Sintered NdFeB magnet production remains limited.
- Frameless torque motors remain under development.
- Robot-grade precision drives remain limited.

Magnets
- India imports ~95% rare-earth magnets.
- Government scheme targets 6,000 tonnes annually.
- NAN GreenMet targets 1,200 tonnes initially.
- Permanent Magnets has phased capacity plans.
- Midwest has announced additional capacity.
- Robot-grade magnet qualification remains unproven.
- Grain-boundary diffusion remains a key gap.

Motors
- India has strong motor-component capabilities.
- CG Power manufactures industrial motors.
- Bharat Bijlee makes AC servo motors.
- Pitti Engineering supplies motor components.
- KSH International supplies magnet winding wire.
- Frameless torque motors remain under development.

Reducers
- Reducers are a major capability gap.
- Indian gear manufacturing is well established.
- Automotive gear production operates at scale.
- Harmonic and RV reducers remain absent.
- Flexsplines require extreme precision.
- Qualification requires substantial development time.

Precision Machinery
- Precision grinding is another bottleneck.
- Indian gear-grinding availability remains limited.
- RACL has highlighted imported grinding machines.
- Macpower imports specialised grinding equipment.
- Jyoti CNC still imports key components.
- India remains dependent on imported precision equipment.

Potential Indian Participants
- Amber Enterprises has BLDC motor capabilities.
- Avalon has motor-drive capabilities.
- Syrma SGS supports industrial electronics.
- Cyient DLM supports electronics manufacturing.
- Siemens India has automation capabilities.
- Igarashi develops traction motors.
- Sintercom develops motor-related components.
- RIR Power Electronics develops SiC capabilities.
- Timken India provides bearing capabilities.

Capacity Scenario
- 10,000 robots require substantial actuator components.
- 100,000 robots sharply increase reducer demand.
- One million robots create massive component requirements.
- Magnet demand also scales rapidly.
- Existing global qualified capacity could face constraints.
- These are scenario calculations, not forecasts.

Qualification Is The Key
- Factory capacity alone is insufficient.
- Components require OEM qualification.
- Reliability data takes years to establish.
- Precision machines may require long lead times.
- Customer design-ins are critical.
- Qualification could become India's biggest bottleneck.

India By 2030
- Machining capabilities could localise further.
- Gear processes can support actuator supply chains.
- Bearings and windings offer immediate opportunities.
- Electronics assembly could expand further.
- Magnet capacity may become meaningful if projects commission.
- Harmonic reducers remain a major uncertainty.
- Encoders and torque sensors remain gaps.

Potential Opportunity
- India could supply actuator components globally.
- Local companies can target precision sub-components.
- Humanoid OEM localisation could accelerate development.
- Sona Comstar has a NEURA Robotics MoU.
- Commercial volumes and qualification remain unproven.
- Precision manufacturing could be the nearer opportunity.

Key Companies To Watch
- Sona Comstar — robotics development.
- MTAR — precision screw development.
- NAN GreenMet — rare-earth magnets.
- Permanent Magnets — magnet capacity.
- Midwest — magnet expansion.
- Kaynes — semiconductor/OSAT ecosystem.
- CG Power — motors and semiconductor ecosystem.
- Jyoti CNC — precision machine tools.

KEY MONITORABLES
- Sona Comstar robotics qualification milestones.
- NEURA partnership commercialisation.
- MTAR screw certification progress.
- Indian magnet plant commissioning.
- Grain-boundary diffusion capability.
- Domestic gear-grinding machine development.
- Kaynes and CG Semi OSAT ramp-up.
- First meaningful robotics-related revenues.

KEY TAKEAWAY
India already has much of the actuator manufacturing periphery, but the precision core remains largely imported or undeveloped. The opportunity is therefore broader than building humanoid robots: it lies in localising precision machining, motors, gears, bearings, magnets, screws, electronics and eventually reducers, sensors and other qualified actuator components.

What regulators see that investors often ignore 👇

Every time a regulator acts, investors first ask: "How much EPS gets hit?" Regulators ask something else: "Is the market structure fair for the end consumer?" That's a very different lens. 
Thoughts on recent #PBFintech & older #IEX n more

Case in point: Recent change on insurance commissions. The proposed changes effectively aim to reduce distribution costs & curb excessive upfront payouts on some products. Investors see lower margins. Regulators see lower customer acquisition costs & better value for policyholders.

Truth is, hardly anyone argues that insurance has zero mis-selling. Higher upfront commissions have often created incentives to sell what pays the most, not what suits the customer best. If that problem exists, intervention shouldn't be surprising.

The irony is that many investors celebrate efficiency in every industry except their own portfolio holdings. When a regulator targets excess distribution costs, the reaction is often outrage instead of introspection.

Look at insurance expense ratios. Even as the industry scaled up, commission/expense pools as a % of premium remained elevated in several segments. The regulator's job is to ask: why isn't scale translating into lower customer costs?

Learning from MFs TER. Every TER cut was seen as fatal attack. Prediction was: growth will die, distributors will vanish, profit collapse. Instead industry adapted. Players became efficient, direct plans gained share, technology reduced costs, investor participation & AUM surged

Market coupling in power exch. Investors focus: which exchange lose market share. Regulators focus: consumers get better price discovery. Market coupling means bids/orders from all exch get pooled to discover a single price. One price improves efficiency & reduces fragmentation

Could one exchange lose moat? Maybe. But from system perspective, better price discovery, deeper liquidity & lower market distortion are hard to ignore.
Regulators rarely optimize for shareholder returns. They optimize for consumers, market efficiency & long-term public interest

Think about hospitals. If tomorrow there is stricter price regulation, hospital stocks may get hit. As investors we'd feel the pain. But can anyone honestly deny healthcare costs are becoming unaffordable for a large section of Indians?
One may argue India's healthcare is still cheaper than many countries. True. But the person comparing prices globally is not the same person struggling to pay a hospital bill locally.

Markets often assume regulators must protect industry profitability. Regulators believe industries shouldn't fleece poor customers. When public benefit & industry profits collide, the regulator's choice is usually obvious.

That's why stock market reaction is often the last variable in the regulator's decision. If a policy improves consumer outcomes, transparency, affordability or efficiency, temporary shareholder pain rarely changes the outcome.

Tata Group Boardroom Tug of War
Some history repeat; Some history rhyme
30 yrs ago it was Ratan Tata vs Russi Mody. Today, many see shades of that battle in the Chandra vs Noel Tata face-off
Back in the 1990s, Ratan Tata was consolidating authority within a sprawling Tata empire run by powerful Operating entity heads. Russi Mody was among the most influential Tata executives of his era. Larger-than-life personality, huge public profile & massive influence within the group.
Ratan Tata believed Tata Group needed one strategic centre of gravity. Not multiple power centres running individual fiefdoms. Eventually, Russi Mody exited & Ratan Tata tightened control over the conglomerate.
Fast forward three decades.
The debate is again centred around leadership, control & the future direction of Tata Sons. This time its Noel Tata, who chairs Tata Trusts, & N Chandrasekaran, who leads Tata Sons
Key contentions are Chandra’s reappointment as chairman & Tata Sons listing. Noel Tata has opposed both
The striking part? Tata Sons board backed Chandra by a 4:1 vote, while Noel Tata stood opposed
Russi Mody took the battle public. Media interviews, public sparring & headline-grabbing exchanges became part of the story.
Chandra, however, has largely stayed silent in public
Whether history repeats or merely echoes, one thing is clear
Generational change of Tata leadership eventually confronts the same question.

Is India investing enough for future capacity

India is usually described as a consumption economy. Consumption contributes >60% of GDP. But the story becomes incomplete when we ignore what's happening on the investment side and other aspects of our economy

India's Gross Capital Formation is ~32.6% of GDP. Lower than China's ~40%, but China's per capita GDP is several times of India's. Comparing ratios without considering income levels misses the context.

A developing country cannot allocate every ₹ toward factories & infra. A large share of resources must also support the bottom of the pyramid through housing, healthcare, education & welfare.

A harmonious society requires a minimum standard of living for those at the bottom. India is building capacity while simultaneously funding social stability. That's a tougher balancing act than many realize.

So let's move beyond GDP narratives & look at hard physical data. India's share of global GDP is only ~3.5% yet produces roughly 10% of the world's steel. Steel almost 3x our weight in global GDP. Steel isn't consumed for consumption's sake, but goes into factories, rail tracks, power plants, ports, airports, infrastructure etc

Cement tells the same story. India produces ~400 MT annually out of ~4,000 MT globally. Again, roughly 10% global share despite only ~3.5% share of world GDP. Countries don't consume steel & cement at this scale unless they are building physical assets. These are the raw materials of future GDP.

Power generation presents a slightly different picture. India's share of global electricity output is lower than steel & cement, but still materially ahead of its global GDP share. India with 1800bn units vs 32,000bn units, 6% global share

The evidence suggests India is investing for future capability. One may argue the investment cycle started later than it should have, but the direction is unmistakable. Steel, Cement & Power share point toward economy preparing for a much larger future.

The scale of projects are also changing. DFCs, industrial corridors, semiconductor fabs, renewable energy parks, metros, airports, transmission corridors & logistics networks are larger than anything India attempted before.

If this trend continues, India's share of global steel, cement & power usage is likely to keep rising. Higher material intensity today is often a precursor to higher economic output tomorrow.

Maybe the better way to describe India isn't "consumption economy." It's a country simultaneously consuming, uplifting millions & building future productive capacity. 
India need a balancing act of Building future and taking care of the needy, which it is working towards

De-Dollarization lets peek into central bank reserves

Central banks are diversifying but US$ isn't giving up the throne anytime soon. Headlines scream de-dollarization bt US$ still makes up ~57% of global FX reserves. That's down from decades ago, but still miles ahead of everyone else.

Euro is the 2nd largest reserve currency at ~20%. But Europe faces weak growth, aging demographics, fiscal stress & fragmented politics. Hence no comfort for people looking to diversify away from US$

Then its China. Despite its economic size, RMB is only ~2% of global reserves & ~2% of global payments. Clear reflection of trust issues with the dragon. deep capital markets, convertibility & rule of law issues also there

They're moving into something with no issuer at all: Gold. Central banks themselves are now one of the biggest sources of gold demand globally, roughly buy ~30% of annual global mine production

Gold isn't rising only because investors are bullish. Significant chunk of global prodn is locked away by sovereign balance sheets. In 2026, central banks gold buying at slower pace vs 2025 due to 60% price rise.

Among the Major buyers were Poland, China, Brazil, India etc. 
Then there are few sellers too. Turkey has been among the largest sellers this year, reportedly selling ~83t YTD to support liquidity & FX/US$ needs.

That’s the problem. Though world want to move away from US$ in the long term but  issue in the medium term created due to lack of US$ in the country. 
Case in point Turkiye

Russia has also been a notable seller, reducing reserves by ~44t YTD as it seeks hard-currency liquidity. But Russia is also large producer of Gold

Gold is becoming a reserve diversification asset in a world where trust in fiat issuers is fragmenting.
BUT de-dollarization in reserves doesn't mean de-dollarization in trade.
That’s two very different thing

Global trade still run on the USD infrastructure. That network effect is incredibly hard to replace.
So its two-step process. Trade continues in USD.
But exporting nations convert a portion of their accumulated surplus reserves into gold, commodities, sovereign funds or other reserve assets.

The world may keep transacting in dollars while increasingly choosing not to store all its savings in dollars.

Conclusion:
Real story is different from "the end of the USD."
Reserve diversification is real.
Dollar replacement is not. Not in near future

Birla trying to replicate Paint like disruption in Wire & Cables
India's W&C industry is a INR 1.1trn & growing at ~13% CAGR. Despite its size (0.3% of India GDP), industry remains fragmented with top 6 players control ~50% share

Market is roughly split into 3 equal buckets: Wires, LT Cables & MV/HT/EHV/Specialized Cables. Cables compared to wire is more organized, house wires have larger unorganized participation. Overall unorganized is > 30%

what attracted Birla. W&C sits at the intersection of electrification, urbanization & digitization. Housing, infra, renewables, data centres & manufacturing all need more wires.

Ultratech has launched Ultravolt with planned capex of ₹18 bn. Initial plant capacity has already started production ahead of schedule at Bharuch. The market compares this with the paint disruption. Lets look at numbers

Grasim's paint capex was ~65-70% of Asian Paint. Ultravolt's ₹18 bn capex is 30% of Polycab gross block. Plus, Polycab's gross block is expected to reach ~₹94 bn in FY28 while KEI could reach ~₹43 bn. Ultravolt's announced gross block is only ₹18 bn

The biggest advantage for Ultratech is raw material availability. Copper & Aluminium dominate industry economics and the Birla ecosystem already has deep expertise & inhouse production

Demand-intelligence advantage. Cement is purchased 6 months before wires in building construction. Ultratech can potentially spot demand trends 4-6 months ahead of competitors

Builder relationships, contractor network & Ultratech Building Solutions outlets create a ready-made ecosystem for cross-selling wires. That's a powerful advantage most new entrant

Ultravolt has prepared well. Better channel incentives, faster delivery commitments, aggressive marketing & strong retailer engagement are already creating buzz. But replicating the paint playbook won't be straightforward. 

Paints & cement share significant overlap in distribution. Wires are largely sold through electrical dealers, distributors, retailers & electrician networks. Building an electrical distribution franchise takes years

Another key difference is profitability. Leading W&C players operate at ~12-14% EBITDA margins, far lower than the 18-20%+ margins paint Co. enjoyed before disruption. With lower margins, room for aggressive pricing is limited

Further: Utility, industrial, railway, transmission & infra projects require extensive testing, approvals, certifications & execution history before meaningful scale can be achieved.
Conclusion: Birla has genuine advantage in raw material sourcing, builder relationships & demand visibility. But unlike paints, incumbents start with lower margins, stronger technical moats & entrenched distribution

Jury is still out. Ultravolt looks prepared. Space will remain interesting

Coforge Chairman resignation : Lets dig deeper

OP Bhatt's resignation came after disagreements around the Board evaluation process. In his resignation note, he says continuing on Board amid differences regarding his "good faith actions" would not be conducive to Board effective functioning 

OP Bhatt is not a conventional IT industry chairman. He is among India's most respected bankers, having led SBI between 2006-11 & later served on boards across large corporates including Tata Group companies

The market doesn’t take such update kindly, but Bhatt's continuation was already under question even before the resignation. Shareholders (inc largest shareholder Advent) voted against his reappointment as Independent Director from May'27
 
Let’s go a bit in history: The company was earlier known as NIIT Tech before its ownership transition & eventual rebranding to Coforge. Barings acquired control of NIIT in 2020, leading to ownership change then.

Later, Barings steadily monetised its stake through multiple block deals as the company scaled in size, profitability & market value. After Barings' complete exit by FY24, Co. become fully public market institutional owned.

OP Bhatt joined the board in 2024 & became Chairman during a phase when Coforge was pursuing aggressive scale-up ambitions. Coforge accelerated inorganic growth. The acquisition of Cigniti significantly expanded its engineering & digital capabilities under him.

The much bigger acquisition Encora was also under OP Bhatt. The acquisition materially increased Coforge's scale, global delivery footprint & exposure to high-growth digital engineering segments.

Encora also changed the shareholding landscape. Through the transaction, Advent became the largest shareholder in Coforge, making its views impossible for the board to ignore. That's why the key takeaway may not be the resignation itself. The bigger story could be that the largest shareholder & the Chairman were not aligned on important matters. 

The bullish view is that management execution remains intact. The cautious view is that whenever Chairman, Board & largest shareholder are not on the same page, governance questions emerge and mgmt. energy is focussed away from growth.

Impact of change in EV subsidy policy from 31 July 2026

PM E-DRIVE subsidy for electric 2Ws ended on 31 Jul 2026. Govt earlier plan was to support E2W till 31 Mar 2026, then gave the industry a 4-month extension till Jul-end as there was unutilized budget

PM E-DRIVE replaced FAME-II in Oct'24 with a 10,900 Cr outlay. The idea was simple: help EV adoption scale while supporting charging infra, buses, trucks & other EV segments

initially, e-2W buyers got subsidy of 5,000/kWh, capped at 10,000/ vehicle. That was a meaningful discount for mass-market scooters. From Apr'25, cut by half to 2,500/kWh with max capped at 5,000/Veh. Signalling gradual withdrawal of support.

Now for 2W, even that 5,000 support is gone. Effective acquisition cost of an EV scooter will move up. 5,000 price hike may not sound huge, but in entry-level its imp for price-sensitive consumer

Some moderation in electric 2W demand was expected. OEMs were preparing for it as subsidy-led growth gradually transitions to product-led growth. 

August EV 2W market share came lower than July. E2W MS has come down but not in 3w as July subsidy withdrawal only 2W not in 3W. August is typically a non-festival month & seasonality also matters. OEMs should absorb subsidy via better exchange / financing offers

Market is also looking for next phase of EV support. Discussions around "FAME III" continue, but indications suggest focus could shift towards vehicle other than 2W. 2W penetration already >10% while other segment need more support

If electric 2Ws are eventually excluded from future demand subsidies, industry economics will increasingly depend on product quality, distribution, service network & battery costs instead of govt incentives.

One factor often ignored: OEMs capacity are planned in a way where capacity expansion will happen in same facility. Hence, incremental capex intensity will be far lower. Gradual drivetrain shift will continue without large incremental capex

Bottom line: Subsidy withdrawal may create short-term demand noise, but the long-term story remains the same. India's 2W market is enormous, EV penetration is still low, and the migration from ICE to EV is likely to be a long, gradual journey rather than a subsidy-driven sprint.

**FCNR Sugar Rush What does it means for India**
FCNR experiment has turned into a blockbuster. Total inflows exceeded $136bn vs market expectations of ~$80bn. FCNR(B) deposits alone ~$127bn
  
Like Hindi movie, climax was amazing. 
Total inflows were ~$41bn by July-end, ~$73bn by Aug 21 and ~$136bn by Aug 31. Biggest forex mobilization drives India has ever seen. August was where the real frenzy happened. FCNR deposits jumped from ~$65.4bn on Aug 21 to ~$127.2bn by Aug 31.
  
Why did NRIs rush in? RBI effectively removed the pain point: currency hedging cost. Banks offered attractive yields while RBI absorbed swap costs For investors, FCNR became a rare risk-reward opportunity. Attractive $ returns + ability to leverage deposits (leverage run 4-5x)
  
FCNR nuance: Depositor takes bank credit risk but avoids INR depreciation risk since deposits remain in foreign currency. Currency mismatch is largely handled by RBI A key incentive for banks: incremental FCNR funds were exempted from CRR & SLR requirements.
  
More deployable money, less regulatory drag hence higher NIMs, Every $ mobilized can potentially earn better spreads for banks Flip side: Liquidity is now overflowing. System liquidity has surged sharply as these inflows entered the banking system

When banks are flush with money, appetite for wholesale funding drops. That's already showing up in lower CD rates & softer short-term funding costs Excess liquidity usually pushes overnight money market rates lower. Too much cash chasing too few opportunities compress yields
 
The RBI also gets a strategic advantage. Larger forex reserves and dollar balances improve its ability to manage forward market positions & reduce pressure from speculative USD demand. Forward dollar short should be reduced going forward
 
For currency speculator, the message is important. Betting aggressively against ₹ becomes tougher when RBI has significantly larger forex ammunition and stronger external buffers Now comes the hard part. Raising $136bn is the easy part.
  
Deploying it productively is the challenge. These are time-bound liabilities with an embedded cost. Eventually the money must earn more than it costs. INR already showing strength: USDINR below 95 today
 
The success of this scheme won't be judged by the $136bn raised. It will be judged by whether India converts this liquidity windfall into stronger growth, stable ₹, lower funding stress & productive credit creation over the next few years

Is Pvt Banks Really Losing Share vs PSU Banks?

Everyone is talking about PSU banks taking share from Pvt banks. The narrative is simple: PSU banks are growing faster than Pvt banks, so PSU banks are winning. But the reality is a lot more nuanced.

Argument is : PSU banks are fine with 1.0-1.3% RoA vs  Pvt banks target higher profitability. Pvt banks don't want to trade-off profitability for growth.

This has impacted valuations. Premium Pvt bank multiples came with expectation of steadily MS gain vs PSU. Post-Covid, that trend has slowed, creating doubts.

If PSU banks are sacrificing yield for growth, where should it show up first? HFC, safest retail assets with low NPA, Yet PSU bank share has drifted from ~35% in FY21 to ~34% in H1FY26, while Pvt banks have inched up from ~39% to ~40%.

If PSU banks were aggressively chasing growth regardless of return, housing should have been the biggest battleground. The data doesn't show that. PSU gained initially, now plateaued. 

PSU not gainin share from Pvt banks. Market share remained stable, data also inc. HDFC merger boost for pvt bank

So where is PSU growth actually coming from? A large part is Gold Loans.

Many Pvt banks have stayed away from becoming aggressive gold lenders. The business is operationally intensive and risky. PSU banks have been far more active, esp Canara/SBIN. 

Recently, incremental industry gold loan growth has come primarily from PSU banks, increasing their dominance in banking gold-loan AUM.

Second area is Agri lending. PSU banks have stepped up agri lending. May be it’s mandate-driven, or due to deeper reach into semi-urban and rural India where Agri credit demand is.
These segments Pvt banks is not that agressive. PSU banks are gaining share at the system level. But pvt dominance continue in safe mortgages, affluent retail.
